Mount Everest.text: In 1990 Tim Macartney-Snape's team climbed it starting from the Bay of Bengal, almost 700 km away.
Mount Everest.evidence: The closest sea to Mount Everest's summit is the Bay of Bengal, almost 700 km (430 mi) away. To approximate a climb of the entire height of Mount Everest, one would need to start from this coastline, a feat accomplished by Tim Macartney-Snape's team in 1990.

K2.text: Called the Savage Mountain after a 1953 climber said, "It's a savage mountain that tries to kill you."
K2.evidence: K2 became known as the Savage Mountain after George Bell—a climber on the 1953 American expedition—said, "It's a savage mountain that tries to kill you."

Kangchenjunga.text: Its first climbers in 1955 stopped just short of the summit, keeping a promise to the Chogyal of Sikkim.
Kangchenjunga.evidence: It was first climbed on 25 May 1955 by Joe Brown and George Band, who were part of the 1955 British Kangchenjunga expedition. They stopped just short of the true summit, keeping a promise given to Tashi Namgyal, the Chogyal of the Kingdom of Sikkim, that the top of the mountain would remain inviolate.

Lhotse.text: Its name means "South Peak" in Tibetan, reflecting its close relationship with Everest.
Lhotse.evidence: The name Lhotse, which means "South Peak" in Tibetan, further emphasizes the close relationship between the two.

Makalu.text: On the first ascent in 1955, most of the French expedition reached the top, unusual at the time.
Makalu.evidence: Makalu was first summited on May 15, 1955, by Lionel Terray and Jean Couzy of a French expedition led by Jean Franco. ... This was an amazing achievement at the time, to have the vast majority of expedition members summit, especially on such a difficult peak. Prior to this, summits were reached by one to two expedition members at most, with the rest of teams providing logistical support before turning around and heading home.

Cho Oyu.text: Its name means "Turquoise Goddess" in Tibetan, and it is considered the easiest 8,000 m peak to climb.
Cho Oyu.evidence: Cho Oyu means 'Turquoise Goddess' in Tibetan. ... Due to its proximity to this pass and the generally moderate slopes of the standard northwest ridge route, Cho Oyu is considered the easiest 8,000 metre peak to climb.

Dhaulagiri I.text: Its summit rock, like Everest's, is limestone and dolomite formed at the bottom of the ocean.
Dhaulagiri I.evidence: The rock layers found at the summit of Dhaulagiri, as well as Everest, are made up of limestone and dolomite formed at the bottom of the ocean.

Manaslu.text: Its name means "mountain of the spirit"; a Japanese expedition made the first ascent in 1956.
Manaslu.evidence: Manaslu means "mountain of the spirit" and the word is derived from the Sanskrit word manasa, meaning "intellect" or "soul". Manaslu was first climbed on May 9, 1956, by Toshio Imanishi and Gyalzen Norbu, members of a Japanese expedition.

Nanga Parbat.text: Guinness World Records calls it the fastest growing mountain in the world, rising 7 mm a year.
Nanga Parbat.evidence: According to Guinness World Records, Nanga Parbat is the fastest growing mountain in the world, growing taller at a rate of 7 mm (0.27 in) per year.

Annapurna I.text: In 1950 a French expedition made it the first eight-thousander ever climbed.
Annapurna I.evidence: Maurice Herzog led a French expedition to its summit through the north face in 1950, making it the first eight-thousander to be successfully climbed.
